note: Questions from the CBSE Class X Science Term 2 board exam 2022 (40 marks), Q.P. code 31/1/1, published by CBSE at cbse.gov.in. Q2 and Q8 (Periodic Classification, no longer in the syllabus) and questions that need a figure or a drawing (Q6(b), Q11, Q15) are left out. Solutions are written for this portal and are not CBSE's official marking scheme.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) Write the molecular formula of the following carbon compounds : (i) Methane (ii) Propane
(b) Carbon compounds have low melting and boiling points. Why ?
questions.solution: (a) (i) Methane: CH₄. (ii) Propane: C₃H₈. (b) Carbon compounds are covalent; the forces of attraction between their molecules are weak, so little energy is needed to melt or boil them.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) Which of the following flowers will have higher possibility of self-pollination ? Mustard, Papaya, Watermelon, Hibiscus
(b) List the two reproductive parts of a bisexual flower.
questions.solution: (a) Mustard and Hibiscus, because they are bisexual flowers (they have both stamens and pistil); papaya and watermelon flowers are unisexual. (b) Stamen (the male part) and pistil or carpel (the female part).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Which one of the two multicellular organisms Spirogyra and Planaria reproduces by regeneration and why ? Give an example of any other organism which can also reproduce by the same process.
questions.solution: Planaria. It has specialised cells that can divide and form all the different cell types, so if it is cut into pieces, each piece can grow into a complete organism. (Spirogyra reproduces by fragmentation.) Another example: Hydra.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What is variation ? List two main reasons that may lead to variation in a population.
questions.solution: Variation is the difference between individuals of the same species (for example between parents and offspring). Reasons: (1) sexual reproduction, which combines DNA from two different parents; (2) small inaccuracies (errors) in copying DNA.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) In a cross between violet flowered plants and white flowered plants, state the characteristics of the plants obtained in the F₁ progeny.
(ii) If the plants of F₁ progeny are self-pollinated, then what would be observed in the plants of F₂ progeny ?
(iii) If 100 plants are produced in F₂ progeny, then how many plants will show the recessive trait ?
questions.solution: (i) All the F₁ plants have violet flowers (violet is dominant). (ii) The F₂ plants have both violet and white flowers in the ratio 3 : 1. (iii) One quarter of 100, i.e. 25 plants, will show the recessive trait (white flowers).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) Name and state the rule to determine the direction of force experienced by a current carrying straight conductor placed in a uniform magnetic field which is perpendicular to it.
(ii) An alpha particle while passing through a magnetic field gets projected towards north. In which direction will an electron project when it passes through the same magnetic field ?
questions.solution: (i) Fleming's left-hand rule: stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand at right angles to one another. If the forefinger points along the magnetic field and the middle finger along the current, the thumb points in the direction of the force (motion). (ii) An electron has a negative charge, opposite to the positive alpha particle, so it is deflected the opposite way: towards the south.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What is ozone ? How is it formed in the upper layers of the Earth's atmosphere ? How does ozone affect our ecosystem ?
questions.solution: Ozone (O₃) is a molecule made of three oxygen atoms. In the upper atmosphere, high-energy ultraviolet radiation splits O₂ molecules into oxygen atoms (O₂ → O + O), which then combine with O₂ to form ozone (O + O₂ → O₃). The ozone layer protects living things by absorbing harmful UV radiation, which can cause skin cancer and damage organisms.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) List two human-made ecosystems.
(ii) "We do not clean a pond in the same manner as we do in an aquarium." Give reason to justify this statement.
questions.solution: (i) Aquarium, garden (or crop field, park). (ii) A pond is a natural, self-sustaining ecosystem: its decomposers break down wastes and dead remains and recycle nutrients. An aquarium is artificial and lacks enough decomposers, so it has to be cleaned regularly.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Draw two different possible structures of a saturated hydrocarbon having four carbon atoms in its molecule. What are these two structures of the hydrocarbon having same molecular formula called ? Write the molecular formula and the common name of this compound. Also write the molecular formula of its alkyne.
questions.solution: Straight chain: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃ (n-butane). Branched chain: CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₃ (isobutane, 2-methylpropane). Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structures are called structural isomers. Molecular formula C₄H₁₀, common name butane. The alkyne with four carbons is butyne, C₄H₆.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) Write the molecular formula of benzene and draw its structure.
(ii) Write the number of single and double covalent bonds present in a molecule of benzene.
(iii) Which compounds are called alkynes ?
questions.solution: (i) C₆H₆; a hexagonal ring of six carbon atoms with alternate single and double bonds, each carbon bonded to one hydrogen. (ii) 9 single covalent bonds (3 C–C and 6 C–H) and 3 double bonds (C=C). (iii) Alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with at least one carbon–carbon triple bond (general formula CₙH₂ₙ₋₂).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) Mention one function each of the following organs in human male reproductive system : (i) Testis (ii) Scrotum (iii) Vas deferens (iv) Prostate gland
(b) Name the type of germ cell which (i) is motile, and (ii) stores food.
questions.solution: (a) (i) Testis: produces sperms and the hormone testosterone. (ii) Scrotum: keeps the testes outside the abdomen at a slightly lower temperature, which sperm formation needs. (iii) Vas deferens: carries sperms from the testis towards the urethra. (iv) Prostate gland: adds fluid that nourishes the sperms and makes their transport easier. (b) (i) The male germ cell (sperm) is motile. (ii) The female germ cell (egg or ovum) stores food.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) Define Electric Power and write its SI unit.
(ii) Two bulbs rated 100 W; 220 V and 60 W; 220 V are connected in parallel to an electric mains of 220 V. Find the current drawn by the bulbs from the mains.
questions.solution: (i) Electric power is the rate at which electrical energy is consumed (or dissipated) in a circuit; its SI unit is the watt (W). (ii) In parallel each bulb gets 220 V. I = P/V: 100/220 + 60/220 = 160/220 = 8/11 A ≈ 0.73 A.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) State Joule's law of heating. Express it mathematically when an appliance of resistance R is connected to a source of voltage V and the current I flows through the appliance for a time t.
(ii) A 5 Ω resistor is connected across a battery of 6 volts. Calculate the energy that dissipates as heat in 10 s.
questions.solution: (i) The heat produced in a resistor is directly proportional to the square of the current, to the resistance and to the time for which current flows: H = I²Rt (= VIt = V²t/R). (ii) H = V²t/R = (6 × 6 × 10)/5 = 72 J.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) Name the group of organisms which form in the first trophic level of all food chains. Why are they called so ?
(b) Why are the human beings most adversely affected by bio-magnification ?
(c) State one ill-effect of the absence of decomposers from a natural ecosystem.
questions.solution: (a) Producers (green plants and other autotrophs). They make food from simple inorganic substances using sunlight, and this food supplies energy to all other organisms. (b) Human beings are at the top of many food chains, where the concentration of harmful non-biodegradable chemicals is the highest. (c) Dead remains and wastes would pile up and nutrients would not be returned to the soil, so the soil would lose fertility.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
The mechanism by which the sex of an individual is determined is called sex-determination. In human beings, sex of a newborn is genetically determined, whereas in some others it is not. There are 46 (23 pairs) chromosomes in human beings. Out of these, 44 (22 pairs) control the body characters and 2 (one pair) are known as sex chromosomes. The sex chromosomes are of two types — X chromosome and Y chromosome. At the time of fertilisation, depending upon which type of male gamete fuses with the female gamete, the sex of the newborn child is decided.

Why is a pair of sex chromosomes in human beings called a mismatched pair in terms of type and size ?
questions.solution: In males the sex chromosomes are of two different types, X and Y, and the Y chromosome is much shorter than the X. So they differ in both type and size.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
In human beings, there are 46 (23 pairs) chromosomes. Out of these, 2 (one pair) are known as sex chromosomes, of two types — X chromosome and Y chromosome.

Out of male or female, which of them has a perfect pair of sex chromosomes ? In case of a perfect pair, will the gametes produced be of the same kind or of a different kind ?
questions.solution: The female has a perfect pair (XX). All her gametes (eggs) are of the same kind: each carries an X chromosome.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
The mechanism by which the sex of an individual is determined is called sex-determination. In human beings, sex of a newborn is genetically determined, whereas in some others it is not.

Name two animals whose sex is not genetically determined. Explain the process of their sex determination.
questions.solution: For example, some reptiles (such as turtles) and snails. In some reptiles, the temperature at which the fertilised eggs are kept decides whether the young will be male or female. Some animals such as snails can change sex, so their sex is not fixed genetically.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
In human beings, sex of a newborn is genetically determined. At the time of fertilisation, depending upon which type of male gamete fuses with the female gamete, the sex of the newborn child is decided.

With the help of a flowchart only, show how sex is genetically determined in human beings.
questions.solution: Mother (XX) → eggs: all X. Father (XY) → sperms: X or Y. Egg X + sperm X → XX → girl. Egg X + sperm Y → XY → boy.
